title: Normalized deformation comparisons commute with coefficient reduction
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $r\geq m\geq1$, $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$, $B=\mathbf Z/\ell^m\mathbf Z$, and $S$ a Noetherian scheme (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]) on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $g:V\to S$ be smooth separated of finite type and pure relative dimension $d\geq0$, and let $s:S\hookrightarrow V$ be a closed regular section of codimension $d$. Assume the normal bundle $\pi:N_s\to S$ and deformation family $\widetilde g:D\to\mathbf A^1_S$, with section $\widetilde s$, and their compactifiability hypotheses are those specified in [lem-pur-noetherian-etale-section-specialization]. For $R=A,B$, work in the ordinary etale $R$-module derived categories; put $C_R=s^*\omega_{g,R}$ and $F_R=\widetilde s^*\omega_{\widetilde g,R}$, with $\omega_{h,R}=h_R^\times R_{\operatorname{target}(h)}$. Write $a:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$ and $i_j:S\to\mathbf A^1_S$ for $t=j$, $j=0,1$. Let $\kappa_R:F_R\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C_R$ be the normalized isomorphism whose restriction at $1$ is the identity, and put $\delta_R=(i_0^*\kappa_R)^{-1}:C_R\to z^*\omega_{\pi,R}$. Write $S_T=(-)\otimes_A^LB$. For any morphisms
$$e_F:S_{\mathbf A^1_S}F_A\to F_B,\qquad e_C:S_SC_A\to C_B$$
whose restrictions at $t=1$ agree under the canonical fibre identifications, one has
$$\kappa_B\circ e_F=a^*e_C\circ S_{\mathbf A^1_S}(\kappa_A).$$
With $e_0=i_0^*e_F$ under the normal-fibre identifications, this implies
$$\delta_B\circ e_C=e_0\circ S_S(\delta_A).$$
The morphisms $e_F,e_C,e_0$ are not required to be invertible. More generally, restriction along $i_1$ is injective on morphisms $a^*L\to a^*M$ for finite locally constant $B$-module sheaves $L,M$ locally free of rank one on $S$, and on morphisms between their equal shifts in the ordinary derived category.

source.place: Gluing: uniqueness of normalized rank-one comparisons on connected geometric affine-line fibres; extended from isomorphisms to morphisms as in returned item Step 6

proof.text: Since $g$ is of finite type and $S$ is Noetherian, $V$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], so all hypotheses of [lem-pur-noetherian-etale-section-specialization] hold. Apply it separately for $R=A$ and $R=B$. It gives that $F_R[-2d]$ and $C_R[-2d]$ are locally constant free rank-one ordinary étale $R$-module sheaves. Since these sheaves are locally free, derived tensor with $B$ is concentrated in degree zero. The canonical tensor/pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies $S_{\mathbf A^1_S}a^*C_A$ with $a^*S_SC_A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], after cancelling the common shift $[2d]$, equality of the derived maps in the claim is equivalent to equality of the corresponding ordinary sheaf maps.

source.place: Gluing paragraph: both family and section objects are shifts of locally constant rank-one sheaves; morphisms are ordinary sheaf maps

proof.text: Set $u=\kappa_B\circ e_F$ and $v=a^*e_C\circ S_{\mathbf A^1_S}(\kappa_A)$. Their restrictions at $t=1$ agree by hypothesis. After Step 1, cancel $[2d]$ and use $\kappa_A$ to regard $u-v$ as a map $a^*L\to a^*M$ of finite locally constant $B$-module sheaves on $\mathbf A^1_S$, where $L=S_SC_A[-2d]$ and $M=C_B[-2d]$. Let $H$ be the endomorphism of $a^*(L\oplus M)=a^*L\oplus a^*M$ whose diagonal components are $1_{a^*L}$ and $1_{a^*M}$, whose component $a^*L\to a^*M$ is $u-v$, and whose component $a^*M\to a^*L$ is $0$. Its restriction at $t=1$ is the identity. Pulling to the pro-étale sites, [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin] makes $\nu_S^*(L\oplus M)$ a finite locally constant sheaf, [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies the pullback with the affine-line pullback there, and [lem-pur-a1-pullback-endomorphism-rigidity] forces $\nu^*H=1$. The finite-level comparison unit [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] is an isomorphism, so it reflects equality of the original étale maps. Hence $u=v$, proving the first displayed compatibility.

source.place: Gluing paragraph: normalized maps agree on overlaps because their difference is an automorphism of a rank-one locally constant sheaf fixed at t=1

proof.text: Restrict the equality of Step 2 along $i_0$. Writing $x_R=i_0^*\kappa_R$, the fibre comparison gives $x_B\circ e_0=e_C\circ S_Sx_A$. Since each $x_R$ is an isomorphism, left multiplication by $x_B^{-1}=\delta_B$ and right multiplication by $(S_Sx_A)^{-1}=S_S\delta_A$ yield $\delta_B\circ e_C=e_0\circ S_S(\delta_A)$.

source.place: Restriction of the normalized comparison to t=0 and inversion

proof.text: The same matrix argument proves the final general assertion. For arbitrary finite locally constant $B$-module sheaves $L,M$ on $S$, two maps $a^*L\to a^*M$ equal at $i_1$ have difference $q$; the endomorphism of $a^*(L\oplus M)$ with diagonal components the identities, component $q:a^*L\to a^*M$ and zero component $a^*M\to a^*L$ restricts to the identity at $i_1$. The comparison and rigidity statements used in Step 2 force $q=0$. For equal shifts of these sheaves, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] identifies derived maps with the sheaf maps after cancelling the common shift, so restriction along $i_1$ remains injective in the derived category.

Generic full faithfulness of degree-zero sheaves identifies the derived maps after the common shift is removed.
Generic ordinary-to-pro-etale transfer supplies finite locally constant pro-etale sheaves to which affine-line rigidity applies.
Generic comparison pullback coherence identifies the pro-etale pullback of the ordinary affine-line pullback.
Arbitrary-base affine-line endomorphism rigidity is the black-box uniqueness input for the matrix argument.
